chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, altogether from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub from Jameel ibn Salih from one of the companions of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding two sisters who were gifted to two brothers in one night, so the wife of this one was entered to that one, and the wife of that one was entered to this one. He (peace be upon him) said: For each of the two is the dower with the copulation, and if their guardian deliberately did that, the dower would be fined, and each of the two would not go near his wife until the waiting period has expired. So when the waiting period has expired, each one of them would return to her husband with the first marriage.

It was said to him: If they die before the expiration of the waiting period? He said: The two husbands would return half the dower to their heirs, and the two men would inherit them. It was said: If the two men died while they were in the waiting period? He said: They would inherit them both, and for both of them is half the specified dower, and upon them is the waiting period after they finish from the first waiting period. They would observe the waiting period of the one whose husband died.
ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic legal rulings for exchanging two sisters in marriage regarding dower, waiting period, and inheritance?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the fiqh of 'exchange of wives' (tabdil al-nisa'), a specific scenario where two sisters are given to two brothers and their marital consummation is swapped. It establishes that the dower (mahr) is earned through actual consummation, outlines the waiting period (iddah) for the women, and specifies inheritance and dower distribution in cases where either the women or the men die during the waiting period.
